public_notes.title: A Texas History And Restoration
public_notes.text: The Tribe traces Alabama and Coushatta ancestors to neighbouring areas in what is now Alabama, followed by movement into East Texas. Its account places members alongside Sam Houston's army in 1836 as guides and providers for refugees. Its timeline records federal recognition being restored in 1987. Restoration marks a change in legal status; it does not date the people's origins. This is the Tribe's own account of its history. The source gives inconsistent migration dating, so no exact migration year is asserted here.

public_notes.title: Living Government And Community Services
public_notes.text: Today's Tribe describes an elected Council with three-year terms and advisory Chiefs. Its government page also links its Constitution and By Laws, allowing readers to begin with the Tribe's own institutional account. The public services directory lists education, cultural programmes, environmental work and a health clinic alongside other departments. Those listings show where the Tribe directs enquiries, not proof of eligibility, available funding or service outcomes. This profile follows the Alabama-Coushatta Tribe of Texas as a distinct government; it does not substitute for the Coushatta Tribe of Louisiana or every Alabama and Coushatta community.
